## 🎯 Objectives

By the end of this workshop, you will be able to:

* construct a Shiny `tabsetPanel()` from several `tabPanel()` components;
* connect outputs in different tabs to shared reactive calculations;
* use the selected tab as a reactive input;
* move the user to a tab with `updateTabsetPanel()`; and
* show controls only when they are relevant to the active tab.

::: {.callout-important}
## What you will build

You will turn the Week 10 solar app into a four-tab dashboard. Three tabs reserve space for different views of the results. A fourth tab exposes an interval-by-interval calculation trace.

The focus today is the **technical structure** of a multi-tab app. The tutorial will build the detailed content inside the tabs.
:::

## Preparation

Download the [tutorial starter app](../tutorial/starter_app.R) and [household energy data](../tutorial/solar_data.csv). Save them in the same folder.

Make a copy of `starter_app.R` called `workshop_app.R`. Work in the copy so that you can compare your code with the supplied starter later.

Run the app once before changing anything.

::: {.callout-tip}
Run the app after every stage. If it stops working, the most recent edit is the first place to look.
:::

## 1. Trace the existing reactive structure (5 minutes)

Locate these three reactive expressions in `server()`:

~~~r
scenario_data()
metrics()
daily_data()
~~~

Draw arrows showing which reactive calls which:

> inputs · `scenario_data()` · `metrics()` · `daily_data()` · outputs

Then answer:

1. Which reactive performs the interval solar and battery calculations?
2. Which reactive aggregates interval rows into daily rows?
3. If the system-size slider changes, which objects become invalidated?
4. Why should a tab call these reactives instead of rebuilding the scenario itself?

::: {.unilur-solution}
The main dependency paths are:

~~~text
inputs ──> scenario_data() ──> metrics() ──> text/table outputs
                    │
                    └────────> daily_data() ──> plot outputs
                                  │
                    metrics() ────┘
~~~

`scenario_data()` performs the interval calculations. `daily_data()` aggregates the interval rows. A system-size change invalidates `scenario_data()` and therefore every downstream reactive and output that uses it.

Reusing these reactives gives every tab the same scenario and avoids duplicated calculation code.
:::

## 2. Reconstruct the tabset (7 minutes)

Inside `mainPanel()`, replace the existing `tabsetPanel()` with an empty four-tab structure:

~~~r
tabsetPanel(
  id = "dashboard_tab",
  tabPanel("Why invest"),
  tabPanel("Energy balance"),
  tabPanel("Cautious case"),
  tabPanel("Evidence")
)
~~~

Run the app and check that:

* four tabs appear;
* clicking a tab changes the selected panel; and
* the sidebar remains visible because it sits outside the tabset.

Add a short placeholder to each of the first three panels. Use indentation to make the UI hierarchy easy to see.

::: {.unilur-solution}
~~~r
tabsetPanel(
  id = "dashboard_tab",
  tabPanel(
    "Why invest",
    h3("Sales view"),
    p("This tab will be completed in the tutorial.")
  ),
  tabPanel(
    "Energy balance",
    h3("Neutral view"),
    p("This tab will show the daily energy balance.")
  ),
  tabPanel(
    "Cautious case",
    h3("Cautious view"),
    p("This tab will be completed in the tutorial.")
  ),
  tabPanel(
    "Evidence",
    h3("Calculation trace")
  )
)
~~~

The `id` makes the selected tab available in the server as `input$dashboard_tab`. Each tab's title is its value unless a separate `value` is supplied.
:::

## 3. Connect the neutral tab to existing outputs (8 minutes)

The starter server already creates:

* `output$neutral_headline`;
* `output$neutral_message`; and
* `output$neutral_plot`.

Place the matching output functions inside the **Energy balance** tab:

~~~r
h3(textOutput("neutral_headline", inline = TRUE))
textOutput("neutral_message")
plotOutput("neutral_plot", height = "430px")
~~~

Run the app and change the system size and date range.

For each of the three outputs, write down:

| UI placeholder | Server renderer | Shared reactive used |
|---|---|---|
| `textOutput("neutral_headline")` | | |
| `textOutput("neutral_message")` | | |
| `plotOutput("neutral_plot")` | | |

::: {.unilur-solution}
| UI placeholder | Server renderer | Shared reactive used |
|---|---|---|
| `textOutput("neutral_headline")` | `renderText()` | none: the text is currently fixed |
| `textOutput("neutral_message")` | `renderText()` | `metrics()` |
| `plotOutput("neutral_plot")` | `renderPlot()` | `daily_data()` |

An output ID is a contract between the UI and server. For example, `plotOutput("neutral_plot")` must match `output$neutral_plot <- renderPlot({...})` exactly.
:::

Deliberately change one UI ID to `"neutral_plots"`. Run the app, observe the empty space, and then repair the ID.

## 4. Add a calculation-trace tab (9 minutes)

The **Evidence** tab will help you inspect the calculation that feeds every other tab.

Add this placeholder to that tab:

~~~r
tableOutput("calculation_trace")
~~~

In `server()`, create `output$calculation_trace` with `renderTable()`. It should:

1. call `scenario_data()`;
2. keep the first eight rows; and
3. display the time, observed consumption, modelled solar, net demand, battery state, grid import and grid export.

Round numeric values to two decimal places.

::: {.unilur-solution}
Add this to `server()`:

~~~r
output$calculation_trace <- renderTable({
  scenario_data() |>
    slice_head(n = 8) |>
    transmute(
      Time = format(datetime, "%d %b %H:%M"),
      Consumption = round(energy_kwh, 2),
      Solar = round(solar_kwh, 2),
      `Net demand` = round(net_demand_kwh, 2),
      Battery = round(battery_state_kwh, 2),
      Import = round(grid_import_kwh, 2),
      Export = round(grid_export_kwh, 2)
    )
})
~~~

This output exposes intermediate values but does not create a second version of the calculation. It reads from the same `scenario_data()` used elsewhere.
:::

Change the date range and confirm that the first timestamp in the trace changes.

## 5. Treat the selected tab as an input (7 minutes)

Because the tabset has an ID, Shiny stores the selected tab in `input$dashboard_tab`.

Add this immediately before `tabsetPanel()`, then render its value in the server:

~~~r
verbatimTextOutput("active_tab")

output$active_tab <- renderText({
  paste("Active tab:", input$dashboard_tab)
})
~~~

Now add an action button near the top of `mainPanel()`, immediately before `tabsetPanel()`:

~~~r
actionButton("show_evidence", "Inspect the calculation")
~~~

Use `observeEvent()` and `updateTabsetPanel()` to move to the Evidence tab when the button is clicked.

::: {.unilur-solution}
Add this to `server()`:

~~~r
observeEvent(input$show_evidence, {
  updateTabsetPanel(
    session,
    inputId = "dashboard_tab",
    selected = "Evidence"
  )
})
~~~

There are two reactive directions here:

* a user click changes `input$dashboard_tab`; and
* the server can change the selected tab with `updateTabsetPanel()`.

The `selected` value must match the tab title or its explicit `value`.
:::

Test the button from each of the other three tabs.

## 6. Show a control only on the relevant tab (6 minutes)

Add this inside `sidebarPanel()`:

~~~r
conditionalPanel(
  condition = "input.dashboard_tab == 'Evidence'",
  sliderInput(
    "trace_rows",
    "Rows in calculation trace",
    min = 4,
    max = 48,
    value = 8,
    step = 4
  )
)
~~~

Update the calculation table so that it uses `input$trace_rows` instead of always showing eight rows.

::: {.unilur-solution}
The first part of the table code becomes:

~~~r
output$calculation_trace <- renderTable({
  scenario_data() |>
    slice_head(n = input$trace_rows) |>
    transmute(
      # the same columns as before
    )
})
~~~

`conditionalPanel()` is evaluated in the browser, so its condition uses JavaScript syntax. The input still exists while hidden; hiding a control does not remove its value from the server.
:::

Confirm that the slider appears only on the Evidence tab and that it changes the number of table rows.

## 7. Technical check before the tutorial (3 minutes)

Test the finished app systematically:

| Test | Expected result |
|---|---|
| Select each tab | The correct panel appears |
| Change system size | Neutral outputs and trace update |
| Change date range | Plot, message and trace update |
| Click **Inspect the calculation** | Evidence becomes active |
| Move the trace-row slider | Table length changes |
| Exclude the battery | Battery state becomes zero |

Then search your server code for `add_solar_model(` and `dispatch_battery(`. Each should be called only inside `scenario_data()`.

::: {.callout-important}
A tab is a container, not a separate app. The dashboard should have one input state and one calculation pipeline, with several outputs reading from it.
:::

## Extension

Give each tab a short internal value that is independent of its displayed label:

~~~r
tabPanel("Energy balance", value = "neutral", ...)
~~~

Update the conditional panel and `updateTabsetPanel()` call to use the new values. This makes it possible to change the visible tab labels later without breaking server logic.
